title: Падение на лестнице  (The Fall on the Stairs)

segments.t: Drunk Nagiyev wanders back into the hotel insisting he cannot go home while the commission is visiting. As Mikhail tries to shake him sober on the staircase, inspector Pavel Vladimirovich intervenes to defend the guest—and gets accidentally knocked down the stairs.
Простите, я ненадолго отойду.
Позже к вам присоединюсь.
Витя, я не могу домой!
У нас же комиссия в отеле.
Соберись, я тебе говорю!
Что вы себе позволяете?
Как вы обращаетесь с гостями?
Ему стало плохо, я пытался привести его в чувство.
Вы в порядке? А почему вы ругаетесь на этого милого человека?
Кто вам дал право повышать на него голос?
Успокойтесь! Отойдите от меня!
Извините!
Now let's go back through their conversation line by line and unpack the Russian phrasing.
Простите, я ненадолго отойду.
'Excuse me, I will step away for a moment.' Explaining that he will step away for a moment lays the cards on the table for the inspector.
Позже к вам присоединюсь.

'I will join you later.' Mikhail mentions that he will join the inspector later so the inspector sees what is at stake. Notice how he sticks to the formal "you", keeping a professional line between them.
Витя, я не могу домой!
'Vitya, I cannot go home!' Declaring that he cannot go home brings Nagiyev's temper right to the surface. Russian puts the key word right up front so his emotion lands on the first beat.
У нас же комиссия в отеле.
'We have a commission in the hotel.' Explaining that they have a commission in the hotel lays the cards on the table for the inspector.
Соберись, я тебе говорю!

'Pull yourself together, I am telling you!' Saying that the inspector should pull themselves together he is telling the inspector is how Mikhail takes charge of the moment. Using the informal "you" shows how direct and unfiltered their kitchen relationship is.
Что вы себе позволяете?

'What are you allowing yourself?' Here asking what Mikhail allowing themselves is shows the inspector looking for the real truth. Notice how he sticks to the formal "you", keeping a professional line between them.
Как вы обращаетесь с гостями?
'How are you treating the guests?' By wondering how Mikhail treating the guests is, the inspector presses Mikhail for a straight answer.
Ему стало плохо, я пытался привести его в чувство.
'He felt ill, I was trying to bring him to his senses.' Even though he felt ill he was trying to bring him to his senses, Mikhail keeps a steady face in front of the inspector.
Вы в порядке? А почему вы ругаетесь на этого милого человека?

'Are you alright? And why are you yelling at this nice man?' Checking whether Mikhail alright is how the inspector puts Mikhail on the spot. Even in the middle of the drama, he keeps the polite plural "you" that workplace Russian expects.
Кто вам дал право повышать на него голос?
'Who gave you the right to raise your voice at him?' Asking whether who gave Mikhail the right to raise Mikhail's voice at him puts Mikhail right on the defensive.
Успокойтесь! Отойдите от меня!
'Calm down! Step away from me!' Stepping away from him is Mikhail's blunt reaction in front of the inspector. Russian puts the key word right up front so his emotion lands on the first beat.
Извините!

'Excuse me!' Once the inspector should excuse him, Nagiyev makes sure the inspector hears every word. Russian puts the key word right up front so his emotion lands on the first beat. Alright, let's hear the entire conversation one more time from start to finish.
Простите, я ненадолго отойду.
Позже к вам присоединюсь.
Витя, я не могу домой!
У нас же комиссия в отеле.
Соберись, я тебе говорю!
Что вы себе позволяете?
Как вы обращаетесь с гостями?
Ему стало плохо, я пытался привести его в чувство.
Вы в порядке? А почему вы ругаетесь на этого милого человека?
Кто вам дал право повышать на него голос?
Успокойтесь! Отойдите от меня!
Извините!
That brings the staircase confrontation to a close. Listen for the polite plural imperatives meaning calm down and step away from me right before the accident. See you next time!
Увидимся!
